papers.title_en: Geometric Configurations of Perturbed Jailbreak Prompts
papers.authors: Lynn Delcon, Andres Algaba, Vincent Ginis
papers.evidence: 大语言模型中扰动越狱提示词的内部表示研究
papers.tldr: 本研究探讨了扰动越狱提示词在Qwen-2.5和Llama-3.2/3.1等模型内部的几何表示。通过分析最后一层嵌入空间和预测概率空间，发现嵌入空间主要按拼写和格式区分提示词，而概率空间呈现一维特性。研究指出在拒绝回答占主导的数据集中不存在明显的行为超平面，仅特定Token与合规回答有显著关联，为理解大模型安全防御机制提供了几何视角。
papers.abstract_en: Perturbation techniques that turn unsuccessful jailbreak prompts into successful ones are continuously evolving, constituting a major security threat to LLM safety. In this paper, we investigate the internal representations of such string-level perturbed jailbreak inputs in the small weight models of the Qwen-2.5-1.5B/-3B/-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-1B/-3B/-3.1-8B-Instruct families. We select two representation spaces: the last-layer-last-token embedding space and the top-50 next-token probability space. The former space separates prompts based on their spelling and format, while the latter space is effectively one-dimensional but appears more complex to cluster. Within our refusal-dominated answer set we find no behavioral hyperplane in either space. Only the next token "Sure" in the 1.5B Qwen model, and both tokens "," and "ĊĊ" in the 1$ Llama model, display a significant association with a compliant-labeled answer.

papers.title_en: Towards an Automated Test of LLM Security Knowledge
papers.authors: Shufan Chai, Liangliang Sun, Jessica Staddon
papers.evidence: 大语言模型安全知识与漏洞的自动化测试
papers.tldr: 随着大语言模型在安全领域的应用日益增多，评估其安全知识水平变得至关重要。目前主流的评估方法依赖于人工构建的基准测试，耗时且需要专家参与。本文提出了一种半自动化的评估方法，利用消费者保护机构（CPA）的权威信息，通过识别模型回答中的不稳定性来发现知识盲点。在身份盗窃和冒充诈骗两个主题上对Gemini和GPT系列模型进行测试，证明该方法能有效区分模型是否具备足够的安全知识，为LLM安全能力评估提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for a range of software, hardware and human-centered security tasks. Consequently, LLM performance on security tasks is an active area of measurement and research, often with a focus on identifying areas in which LLM security ``knowledge'' may be insufficient. Popular strategies for identifying LLM security knowledge gaps include building corpora of challenge questions or task benchmarks, strategies that require substantial manual work and security expertise to design and execute. We introduce a partially-automated method for assessing LLM knowledge of a security area.The method uses authoritative information from Consumer Protection Agencies (CPAs) to identify instability in LLM responses that can be indicative of knowledge gaps. We demonstrate the method for 2 security topics, identity theft and impostor scams, and 5 LLMs in 2 leading LLM families, Gemini and GPT, using publicly available information about identity theft and impostor scams from 6 CPAs.The method distinguishes between models that have and don't have sufficient knowledge to accurately identify the security topics in text narratives.

papers.title_en: Towards an Automated Test of LLM Security Knowledge
papers.authors: Shufan Chai, Liangliang Sun, Jessica Staddon
papers.evidence: 大语言模型安全知识与漏洞的自动化测试
papers.tldr: 本研究针对大语言模型（LLM）在安全任务中知识评估成本高、依赖人工的问题，提出了一种半自动化的测试方法。该方法利用消费者保护机构（CPA）的权威数据，通过分析模型在处理特定安全叙述时的响应不稳定性，来识别其知识盲区。在对Gemini和GPT系列模型的实验中，该方法有效评估了模型对身份盗窃和冒充诈骗的识别能力，为自动化衡量LLM安全专业知识提供了新思路。

papers.title_en: Broken Gates: Re-evaluating Web Bot Defenses in the Age of LLM Agents
papers.authors: Behzad Ousat, Nikita Turkmen, Lalchandra Rampersaud, Dillan Bailey, Amin Kharraz
papers.evidence: 用于网络机器人攻击的大语言模型智能体及防御评估
papers.tldr: 本研究评估了在LLM智能体时代，现有Web机器人防御系统的有效性。通过对比商业验证码破解服务与多种LLM浏览器智能体，研究发现交互式挑战防御（如hCaptcha、reCaptcha v2）在这些攻击者面前几乎失效。虽然非交互式防御（如reCaptcha v3）表现较好，但其安全性主要依赖于执行环境的真实性而非行为模式。研究揭示了当前防御机制的局限性，为未来机器人管理系统的设计提供了重要参考。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based browser agents are rapidly changing the threat landscape for web security. Unlike traditional automation frameworks that execute predefined scripts, these agents can autonomously navigate websites, reason about page content, and interact with web interfaces using natural-language instructions. This evolution raises fundamental questions about the effectiveness of bot management systems, widely deployed to defend against automated web abuse. In this paper, we present a systematic measurement study evaluating the resilience of both interactive challenge-based defenses and non-interactive trust-based defenses against two attacker classes: commercial Captcha-solving services and LLM-based browser agents. Our evaluation spans seven solver services and six agents, including cloud-hosted, self-hosted, AI-assisted, and browser-extension configurations, tested against hCaptcha, reCaptcha v2, reCaptcha v3, and Cloudflare Turnstile. Our results show that challenge-based defenses are broadly ineffective against commercial solvers, which achieve near-perfect bypass at negligible cost. The challenges can similarly be defeated by LLM-based agents when a dedicated solver module is available. Non-interactive defenses such as reCaptcha v3 exhibit stronger resistance, but our analysis reveals that this resilience does not reflect a fundamental security property. Through fine-grained interaction trace analysis, we find that two agents with nearly indistinguishable behavioral footprints yield divergent outcomes, one bypassing the defense and one failing, isolating execution-environment authenticity, rather than agent behavior, as the determining factor. These findings suggest that the security boundary of non-interactive defenses lies at the environment layer, with significant implications for how bot management systems are designed and evaluated.

papers.title_en: From Evaluation to Optimisation: Hierarchy-Aware Training Signals for CWE Prediction in Python
papers.authors: Muntasir Adnan, Manile Srun, Carlos C. N. Kuhn
papers.evidence: 针对代码大语言模型的安全加固与对抗测试
papers.tldr: 本研究探讨了将 ALPHA 基准中的层次感知惩罚项转化为训练信号，以优化 Python 代码的 CWE 漏洞预测。通过对比监督微调、双头分类损失及基于 GRPO 的强化学习，发现监督方法在分布偏移下表现不佳，而强化学习能显著提升性能。实验表明，Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 经优化后在 SVEN 数据集上的惩罚得分降低了约 28%，成功达到其 4.5 倍规模教师模型的水平，证明了直接奖励信号在层次化分类任务中的优越性。
papers.abstract_en: The original ALPHA benchmark introduced a taxonomy-aware penalty for evaluating CWE-level vulnerability prediction in Python and proposed that the penalty could theoretically also serve as a training signal. This paper provides that validation. We compare three delivery mechanisms: supervised fine-tuning, a dual-head classification loss, and reinforcement learning with a dense reward derived from the normalised penalty. We find that supervised approaches consistently regress below the zero-shot baseline under distribution shift, while GRPO succeeds. Our best policy reduces the cumulative ALPHA penalty of Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on Security Hardening and Adversarial Testing (SVEN) dataset by 27.9% under greedy decoding, and by 25.5% under sampled decoding(p = 0.005, Welch's t-test), reaching statistical parity with its 4.5x larger zero-shot teacher. We conclude that the value of a hierarchical penalty as a training signal depends largely on the directness of its delivery.
